report:
**Conclusion:**

Based on current high-quality medical evidence, **ivermectin does not lower the risk of death in COVID-19 patients.**

Although early laboratory (in vitro) studies suggested potential antiviral activity at very high concentrations, large-scale clinical trials and comprehensive systematic reviews demonstrate that standard therapeutic doses of ivermectin provide no mortality benefit.

Key evidence includes:
* **Cochrane Systematic Review:** Comprehensive evaluations of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) found no high-quality evidence supporting the use of ivermectin to reduce all-cause mortality, improve clinical recovery, or prevent COVID-19 infection.
* **Large Randomized Controlled Trials:** Major clinical trials (such as TOGETHER and ACTIV-6) and systematic meta-analyses determined that ivermectin does not reduce hospitalizations or death compared to placebo or standard care.
* **Clinical Guidelines:** Health authorities and advisory bodies, including the National Institutes of Health (NIH), the World Health Organization (WHO), and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), recommend against using ivermectin to treat COVID-19 outside of formal clinical trials.

**Sources:**
* Cochrane Review: https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD015017_ivermectin-preventing-and-treating-covid-19
* NIH COVID-19 Treatment Guidelines: https://www.covid19treatmentguidelines.nih.gov/therapies/miscellaneous-drugs/ivermectin/
* Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0924857924001663
